Thank you all for thorough and candid reports. Let me synthesize what I'm hearing and lay out where I think we land.

First, Noah's finding of the 2019 coexistence letter is pivotal. It means our hands are largely tied on class 42 — the competitor has contracted permission for software use in that class. Second, Maya's confirmed instances of actual customer confusion in the medical-device space strengthen our class 9 position significantly. I'll need that evidence index completed and the records attached to the draft filing package before I give final approval — we need that documentation in the record.

Third, Daniel's conflicts finding is a hard prerequisite I will not waive. We cannot proceed with any filing until the competitor's parent company provides informed written consent and we have an ethical screen in place. I want this flagged as a required sign-off item, and I want confirmation in writing before this office signs off on anything.

So my preliminary direction is this: we scope our filing to opposition of the class 9 application only, we do not challenge class 42, we anchor our evidence of confusion in the medical-device overlap, and we hold all filings until Daniel's conflicts prerequisites are satisfied. Before I formally settle the strategy, does anyone have anything else to add — Maya, will the evidence index be ready within the next 48 hours? And Daniel, what is your realistic timeline for securing the parent company's informed consent and standing up the ethical screen?
